text:
Marathon Petroleum recovered today, gaining 1.78%, after a brutal two-week slide that saw the stock down 10%. The recovery follows mixed signals on geopolitical risk: while Trump said the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon" and oil prices dipped on those peace hopes (Brent briefly fell below $90), the Treasury Secretary was moved to a military base due to Iranian threats, and the Secretary of State said negotiations remain unproductive. Crude has stabilized around $99–107 per barrel, and US refineries are running at 94.5%, so the immediate operating environment hasn't dramatically worsened—the stock may be bouncing after overshooting downward last week.

The broader backdrop here is conflicting signals about Iran risk and energy demand. The midterm elections dealt a setback to the renewable energy push (which could support fuel demand longer-term), but uncertainty about whether de-escalation actually happens is keeping oil and energy stocks volatile. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices can help margins—but the swings in geopolitical risk have dominated recent trading more than the actual fundamentals of refining economics.
